Operational Excellence

Improvement that is still working a year later.

Operational excellence is not a project. Gains fade when improvement lives in projects instead of in the daily running of the operation.

What often goes wrong

  • Kaizen events deliver quick wins that disappear within months.
  • Improvement boards are full, but core KPIs are flat.
  • Nobody checks whether a change is still in place after 30 or 90 days.
  • Improvement depends on a few enthusiasts.

What I do

I link improvement priorities to the measures that matter to the business. I set up simple routines to check results at 30 and 90 days, and build the skills of team leaders so improvement becomes part of the job.

What you get

  • A focused improvement portfolio tied to business measures
  • 30-day and 90-day verification routines
  • Tiered daily and weekly performance reviews
  • Coaching for team leaders and managers

Relevant evidence

Continuous improvement maturity rose from 1.27 to 2.0 in 12 months on the business’s internal assessment. Qualifications include Six Sigma and PRINCE2 Practitioner.

Question

Do we need a Lean programme already in place?

No. The work fits businesses at any stage of maturity.
